messages.author: ede0816c2befa8d7
messages.subject: New user_R-INLA_some inquiry
parts:
Dear R-INLA users,

I am very new to R-INLA package so I have lots of inquires regarding it's implementation.

I have gas data (NO, NO2, NOx, CO, and CO2) that was recorded at 25 monitoring sites across Brisbane. Each site data was recorded for two weeks with resolution of every 30 seconds. 

Now I am planning to implement a spatial model using R-INLA. 

Do you have any suggestion?

How should I start with?

Warm regards,
Mahmud

PhD student, QUT

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] New user_R-INLA_some inquiry
parts:
Hi

I would have a look at the tutorials at

http://www.r-inla.org/examples/tutorials


in the long-one, there is an example of a decreased time resolution
which may be useful in your case.

also this paper might be useful

http://www.r-inla.org/examples/case-studies/cameletti-et-al



Best
H

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] New user_R-INLA_some inquiry
parts:
Hi Håvard,

I'm working with Mahmud on this. We're following the Cameletti et al. example but our data is such that we've got a year's worth of data at a handful of government monitoring sites and then two weeks at most of the other sites (and they don't overlap). In this instance, is it correct that we would want to bulk out our data frame with NAs for the "missing" values where we weren't monitoring at a particular site. If so, do we then just proceed as per the Cameletti work?

Thanks,

Sam Clifford

You should do it with inla.stack and inla.spde.make.A.  Very few NAs should be added manually. 

D
